The longest river in the world is the Nile River.

To help you understand the concept of inflation theory in cosmology, imagine you have a tiny, wrinkled piece of fabric that represents the early universe. Inflation theory suggests that, for a split second right after the Big Bang, this fabric was stretched out incredibly fast—much faster than the speed of light.

Think of it like blowing up a balloon. If you have a small, deflated balloon and you suddenly pump a huge amount of air into it, the surface of the balloon expands rapidly. The wrinkles smooth out, and the surface becomes vast and flat. Similarly, the universe expanded so quickly during this period that it smoothed out and grew to a massive size in a fraction of a second. This rapid expansion explains why the universe looks so uniform and flat today.
